meaning: To be emotionally overwhelmed or deeply moved — your psychological defenses get 'broken through'. Used for anything from being touched to tears to being provoked/triggered.
meaning_zh: 指心理防线被击穿、情绪失控或深受触动——可以是被感动到哭，也可以是被激怒。
example: 看到那条新闻我直接破防了。
example_pinyin: Kàndào nà tiáo xīnwén wǒ zhíjiē pòfáng le.
example_translation: Seeing that piece of news completely broke me.
context: Originally a gaming term (an enemy's defense being penetrated). Netizens repurposed it for emotional 'defenses', and it exploded across Weibo and Bilibili as the go-to way to say something hit you hard.

sources.note: 百度百科 · 破防（2021年网络流行语）
China Daily 语言点：网络流行语“破防”，如何翻译？

meaning: To 'lie flat' — to opt out of relentless striving, reject social pressure to overwork, and settle for a minimal, low-stress life.
meaning_zh: 指放弃拼命奋斗、不再迎合社会压力，选择低欲望、低压力的生活方式。
example: 卷不动了，我选择躺平。
example_pinyin: Juǎn bù dòng le, wǒ xuǎnzé tǎngpíng.
example_translation: I can't keep grinding — I choose to lie flat.
context: A landmark 2021 movement among young Chinese pushing back against '996' overwork culture. Became a cultural lightning rod, even drawing state media commentary. Pairs directly with 内卷.

sources.note: Wikipedia · Tang ping (躺平)
Wiktionary · 躺平

meaning: 'Involution' — pointless, escalating internal competition where everyone works harder and harder for the same or shrinking rewards.
meaning_zh: 指无意义的过度竞争：大家越来越拼命，回报却没有增加，甚至更少。
example: 这个行业太内卷了，加班到半夜也没用。
example_pinyin: Zhège hángyè tài nèijuǎn le, jiābān dào bànyè yě méi yòng.
example_translation: This industry is so involuted — working till midnight doesn't even help.
context: Borrowed from anthropology ('involution'), it went viral among students and white-collar workers to describe zero-sum rat-race competition. The verb form 卷 (juǎn) alone now means 'to compete obsessively'.

sources.note: Wikipedia · Neijuan (内卷)
Queen Mary University of London · Chinese catchwords: 'Involution' (neijuan)

meaning: The GOAT / the best ever. An abbreviation typed in pinyin initials, used to hype up anything you love — a person, a food, a show.
meaning_zh: “永远的神”的拼音缩写，用来夸人或事物最厉害、无可超越。
example: 这家火锅yyds！
example_pinyin: Zhè jiā huǒguō yyds!
example_translation: This hotpot place is the GOAT!
context: Started in esports/livestreaming fandom praising a legendary player, then became universal internet praise. A prime example of the pinyin-initial abbreviations (like xswl, nsdd) that dominate Chinese chat.

meaning: To feel down, melancholy, or in your feelings. Used as a verb: 我emo了 = 'I'm feeling low.'
meaning_zh: 借自英文，指情绪低落、伤感、陷入负面情绪。“我emo了”就是“我心情很低落”。
example: 半夜听这首歌我又emo了。
example_pinyin: Bànyè tīng zhè shǒu gē wǒ yòu emo le.
example_translation: Listening to this song at midnight made me emo again.
context: Borrowed from the English 'emo' subculture but stripped to just mean 'sad/moody'. Peak usage is the late-night '网抑云' (a pun on NetEase Music) phenomenon of posting melancholy comments after dark.

sources.note: 百度百科 · emo（网络流行语）
中国新闻网：满屏都是“我emo了”网友们到底在说些啥？

meaning: An attention-grabbing show-off — someone (or even an animal/object) that's hilariously extra and can't help standing out. Usually affectionate.
meaning_zh: 指特别爱出风头、搞笑又抢眼的人（有时也指动物或物品），多为亲昵的调侃。
example: 我们班的显眼包又在讲笑话了。
example_pinyin: Wǒmen bān de xiǎnyǎnbāo yòu zài jiǎng xiàohuà le.
example_translation: The class clown is telling jokes again.
context: A regional dialect word that went nationwide in 2023 via short-video platforms. Spawned endless '显眼包' compilation videos of goofy pets, kids, and coworkers.

sources.note: 百度百科 · 显眼包（网络流行词）
澎湃新闻：“十大网络流行语”公布：显眼包、特种兵旅游等入选

meaning: 'Is it urban/cool/modern or not?' A playful way to ask if something feels stylish, exciting, or big-city. Often just means 'fun/exciting'.
meaning_zh: 用“是不是”的句式问某样东西“洋气不洋气、刺激不刺激”，常表示“好玩、时髦”。
example: 来上海玩，你说city不city？
example_pinyin: Lái Shànghǎi wán, nǐ shuō city bù city?
example_translation: Come hang out in Shanghai — pretty 'city', right?
context: Coined by an American travel vlogger ('保保熊') touring China in 2024. His half-English catchphrase went massively viral, and 'city' became an adjective for cosmopolitan/exciting. A rare English loanword used in a Chinese grammar pattern.

sources.note: 百度百科 · city不city
新华网：对话“保保熊”揭秘“City不City”背后的故事

meaning: 'So what?' / 'And then what?' A breezy, unbothered comeback that shrugs off criticism or pressure. An attitude of cheerful defiance.
meaning_zh: “那又怎样？”一种满不在乎、轻松反击的态度，不把别人的评价放在心上。
example: 别人说我躺平，那咋了？我开心就行。
example_pinyin: Biérén shuō wǒ tǎngpíng, nà zǎ le? Wǒ kāixīn jiù xíng.
example_translation: People say I'm slacking off — so what? As long as I'm happy.
context: Went viral from a June 2024 Douyin video by blogger 鸭鸭米 — '人生无非三个字：那咋了？' — and became one of 2024's defining catchphrases. The '那咋了文学' (so-what literature) trend resurfaced a year later: a relaxed, thick-skinned refusal to let others' judgements get to you.

sources.note: 百度百科 · 那咋了
搜狐：网络热词“那咋了”，究竟想表达啥？

meaning: A sense of ease and unbothered calm — being relaxed, composed, and not uptight, even when things go sideways.
meaning_zh: 指从容淡定、不紧绷的状态，即使出了状况也能保持轻松自在。
example: 她面对镜头特别有松弛感。
example_pinyin: Tā miànduì jìngtóu tèbié yǒu sōngchígǎn.
example_translation: She's so at ease in front of the camera.
context: Went viral from a 2022 post about a family staying calm after a travel mishap. Became an aspirational aesthetic on 小红书 (RED) — the coveted, effortless 'relaxed vibe' in fashion, lifestyle, and attitude.

sources.note: 百度百科：松弛感（网络流行语）
腾讯新闻：诊断流行情绪：“松弛感”为什么被热议？

meaning: Amazing! / Incredible! An over-the-top exclamation of praise (occasionally used sarcastically for something amazingly bad).
meaning_zh: “太绝了！”极度夸张的赞叹（偶尔也反讽某样东西烂得离谱）。
example: 这个妆容绝绝子！
example_pinyin: Zhège zhuāngróng juéjuézi!
example_translation: This makeup look is absolutely stunning!
context: Popularized by talent-show fan culture and 小红书 reviewers. The '子' suffix and reduplication give it a cutesy, exaggerated tone — a hallmark of a whole family of '-子' internet words.

sources.note: 百度百科：绝绝子
腾讯新闻：“万物皆可绝绝子”：网络用语的暴力逻辑

meaning: Self-inflicted mental exhaustion — burning yourself out through overthinking, self-doubt, and rumination, rather than from any outside pressure.
meaning_zh: 指因过度思虑、自我怀疑而造成的自我消耗和心累，与外部压力无关。
example: 别再内耗了，事情没那么糟。
example_pinyin: Bié zài nèihào le, shìqíng méi nàme zāo.
example_translation: Stop tormenting yourself over it — things really aren't that bad.
context: The inward twin of 内卷: where 内卷 is exhausting external competition, 内耗 is the exhausting war inside your own head. In its fuller form 精神内耗 it was named one of 《咬文嚼字》's top-ten buzzwords of 2022, and it remains a staple of mental-health talk on 小红书 and Weibo.

sources.note: 百度百科：精神内耗（网络流行语）
澎湃新闻：《咬文嚼字》发布2022年十大流行语，精神内耗、烟火气等入选

meaning: The worn-out 'office aura' a job stamps on you — tired eyes, dull clothes, no spark. '一身班味' = reeking of the 9-to-5 grind.
meaning_zh: 指工作在人身上留下的疲惫、暗淡的气息——没精神、没光彩。“一身班味”就是被上班磨得没了朝气。
example: 刚工作半年，我浑身都是班味了。
example_pinyin: Gāng gōngzuò bànnián, wǒ húnshēn dōu shì bānwèi le.
example_translation: Only half a year into the job and I already reek of the office grind.
context: Blew up as young workers joked about losing their pre-job glow. The flip side is '洗掉班味' (washing off the work-smell) — shedding that worn-down look on weekends and holidays. A wry cousin of 躺平 and 内卷.

sources.note: 百度百科：班味
中国作家网：班味、city不city最流行

meaning: The quality of coming across as a real, spontaneous human online — warm and genuine rather than a polished, robotic, over-curated persona. High praise.
meaning_zh: 指在网上显得真实、鲜活、有人情味，而不是精致、刻板、过度包装的人设。
example: 这个博主很有活人感，不像在营业。
example_pinyin: Zhège bózhǔ hěn yǒu huórén gǎn, bù xiàng zài yíngyè.
example_translation: This blogger feels genuinely human — not like they're just 'on the clock.'
context: Named one of 《咬文嚼字》's top-ten buzzwords of 2025, as a reaction to AI-polished images and formulaic, over-produced influencer and celebrity content. Its opposite is 营业 (yíngyè, lit. 'doing business') — performing a role for the camera. To have 活人感 is to feel refreshingly real.

sources.note: 百度百科：活人感
澎湃新闻：谷子、苏超、活人感……哪个是令你印象深刻的“全民流行语”

meaning: 'Emotional value' — the comfort, reassurance, and good feelings a person gives you. '提供情绪价值' = to make someone feel good and supported.
meaning_zh: 指一个人能给你带来的安慰、支持和好心情。“提供情绪价值”就是让对方感到被关心、心情变好。
example: 他很会提供情绪价值，跟他聊天很治愈。
example_pinyin: Tā hěn huì tígōng qíngxù jiàzhí, gēn tā liáotiān hěn zhìyù.
example_translation: He's really good at giving emotional support — chatting with him is so healing.
context: Migrated from psychology and relationship advice into everyday dating and consumer talk, and was named one of the National Language Resources Monitoring and Research Centre's top-ten internet buzzwords of 2025. It's now a core yardstick young people use to judge partners, friendships, and even brands and fandoms.

meaning: A loss may turn out to be a blessing in disguise — you can't always tell good fortune from bad. Full form: 塞翁失马，焉知非福.
meaning_zh: 比喻一时的损失也许反而是好事，福祸难料。完整说法：“塞翁失马，焉知非福”。
example: 丢了这份工作也许是塞翁失马，说不定有更好的机会。
example_pinyin: Diūle zhè fèn gōngzuò yěxǔ shì sài wēng shī mǎ, shuōbudìng yǒu gèng hǎo de jīhuì.
example_translation: Losing this job might be a blessing in disguise — maybe a better chance is on the way.
context: A classic chengyu from the Huainanzi: an old man's horse runs off (a loss), then returns with another horse (a gain), which leads to his son breaking a leg (bad), which then spares him from being drafted into war (good). Netizens still drop it in comment sections to console someone after a setback.

sources.note: 百度百科：塞翁失马
汉典：塞翁失马 词语的基本解释

meaning: To slack off — goof around, look busy, or quietly do nothing while on the clock, whether at work or in a group task.
meaning_zh: 指偷懒：上班或做事时表面忙碌，实则不干正事、划水。
example: 老板不在，大家都在摸鱼。
example_pinyin: Lǎobǎn bù zài, dàjiā dōu zài mō yú.
example_translation: The boss is out, so everyone's slacking off.
context: From the idiom 浑水摸鱼 ('fishing in muddy waters'). Now the go-to word for skiving at work — a whole 摸鱼 culture of memes, payday-countdown apps, and strategic toilet breaks has grown around it.

萌娘百科：摸鱼

meaning: 'Social death' — a moment of public embarrassment so excruciating you wish the ground would swallow you. Short for 社会性死亡.
meaning_zh: “社会性死亡”的简称，指在公众面前极度尴尬、恨不得钻进地缝的时刻。
example: 我叫错了老师的名字，当场社死。
example_pinyin: Wǒ jiào cuò le lǎoshī de míngzì, dāngchǎng shè sǐ.
example_translation: I called the teacher by the wrong name and died of embarrassment on the spot.
context: Full form 社会性死亡. Fuels endless '社死现场' (social-death moment) threads on Weibo and RED where people swap their most cringeworthy public humiliations. Its opposite is 社牛, a fearless social butterfly.

sources.note: 百度百科：社会性死亡
萌娘百科：社会性死亡

meaning: 'Special-forces tourism' — cramming in as many sights as possible on a lightning, bare-bones trip with minimal sleep and money. Maximum sightseeing, minimum rest.
meaning_zh: 指用最少的时间和金钱、几乎不休息地打卡尽可能多的景点的极限旅行方式。
example: 周末我们特种兵旅游，两天逛了五个城市。
example_pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen tèzhǒngbīng lǚyóu, liǎng tiān guàng le wǔ ge chéngshì.
example_translation: We did special-forces tourism this weekend — five cities in two days.
context: A craze among cash-strapped students: overnight trains, dawn starts, ticking off landmarks military-style. Named an official top-ten phrase and still the label for any punishing whirlwind trip.

sources.note: 澎湃新闻："十大网络流行语"公布：显眼包、特种兵旅游等入选
光明网：解码2023年度十大流行语

meaning: A 'mouth substitute' — someone who says out loud exactly what you were thinking but couldn't put into words. Your spokesperson.
meaning_zh: “嘴巴的替身”，指替你说出你想说却说不出来的话的人。
example: 这个博主简直是我的嘴替，说出了我的心声。
example_pinyin: Zhège bózhǔ jiǎnzhí shì wǒ de zuǐtì, shuō chū le wǒ de xīnshēng.
example_translation: This blogger is totally my mouthpiece — they said exactly what I felt.
context: High praise for a commentator or netizen who nails a shared feeling perfectly. '互联网嘴替' (the internet's mouthpiece) is a badge of honor for anyone who voices what everyone's thinking.

sources.note: 百度百科：嘴替
中国作家网：为什么这些词成了互联网"嘴替"

meaning: 'And what can you even do about it?' A deliberately clumsy, sing-song shrug of resignation at life's little annoyances — you can't change it, so why stress.
meaning_zh: “那又能怎么办呢？”一种故意语法不通、无奈又认命的调侃，用来面对生活中的各种烦心事。
example: 周一又来了，如何呢又能怎。
example_pinyin: Zhōuyī yòu lái le, rúhé ne yòu néng zěn.
example_translation: Monday's here again… and what can you even do about it.
context: Grew from 单依纯's divisive, heavily reworked cover of 《李白》 on episode 4 of 《歌手2025》 (June 2025), whose added, much-repeated spoken line '如何呢，又能怎' went viral. Named one of the National Language Resources Monitoring and Research Centre's top-ten internet buzzwords of 2025, it's now tacked onto any complaint — Mondays, plan changes, bad luck — as a comically defeated sigh.

sources.note: 新浪财经："如何呢，又能怎"是什么梗？
新华网：2025年度十大网络流行语发布（国家语言资源监测与研究中心）

meaning: To feed on illusions — to comfort yourself, or fob others off, with empty, unfulfillable promises.
meaning_zh: 比喻用无法兑现的空想或空头承诺来自我安慰或搪塞别人。网络上常简称“画饼”。
example: 老板又在给我们画饼充饥，说年底一定加薪。
example_pinyin: Lǎobǎn yòu zài gěi wǒmen huà bǐng chōng jī, shuō niándǐ yídìng jiāxīn.
example_translation: The boss is dangling empty promises again, saying we'll definitely get a raise at year-end.
context: A classic chengyu (from the Three Kingdoms era) that thrives online as the clipped verb 画饼 (huàbǐng) — now the standard word for a boss serving up grand, hollow promises to keep you working. A 成语 living a second life as office slang.

sources.note: 百度百科：画饼充饥（汉语成语）
汉典：画饼充饥的解释

meaning: An 'unorthodox hack' — a wildly unconventional, even absurd-looking shortcut that actually works. Applied to anything from cooking to fitness to studying.
meaning_zh: 指看似离谱、不按常理出牌，但实际上很管用的非常规方法或技巧，涵盖做饭、健身、学习等各种生活领域。
example: 用蜜雪冰城的柠檬水腌肉，是我摸索出的邪修做饭法。
example_pinyin: Yòng Mìxuě Bīngchéng de níngméngshuǐ yān ròu, shì wǒ mōsuǒ chū de xiéxiū zuòfàn fǎ.
example_translation: Marinating meat in bubble-tea-chain lemonade is my own unorthodox cooking hack.
context: Borrowed from cultivation-fantasy (修仙) novels, where 邪修 are practitioners who reject the orthodox path for faster, riskier power. 小红书 users repurposed it in 2025–2026 for real life: posts like '兴趣邪修' and '邪修做饭' went viral for cutting corners in delightfully weird ways that actually deliver results.

sources.note: 百度百科：邪修（网络流行语）
澎湃新闻："邪修"走红：短平快的实用主义，"向内转"的苦中作乐

meaning: A cheeky twist on 'love yourself' — addressing yourself like an old, familiar friend ('old self') rather than an abstract ideal, said as a bit of self-encouragement or self-care.
meaning_zh: “爱自己”的俏皮说法，把“自己”称作相识多年的“老己”，像哄老朋友一样安慰、鼓励自己，冲淡了传统自爱口号的说教感。
example: 今天又搞砸了，没事，爱你老己，明天见。
example_pinyin: Jīntiān yòu gǎozá le, méishì, ài nǐ lǎo jǐ, míngtiān jiàn.
example_translation: Messed up again today — it's fine, love you old self, see you tomorrow.
context: Riffs on a League of Legends voice line, '爱你老妈，明天见' ('love you mum, see you tomorrow'), swapping in '老己'. It swept social media from late 2025 into 2026, with many hailing it as the year's kindest meme for reframing self-compassion without the usual self-help cheesiness.

sources.note: 澎湃新闻："爱你老己"："有史以来最好的梗"，名副其实吗？
南方网评：爱你老己，为啥是有史以来最好的梗？

meaning: A 'crispy-skinned office worker' — someone who looks fine but is physically fragile, falling ill or getting hurt from the mildest overexertion, like a chip that shatters at a touch.
meaning_zh: 形容看起来正常，实则身体很脆弱的年轻上班族——熬夜加班、稍微劳累一下就生病或受伤，像薯片一样一碰就碎。
example: 加班到凌晨，第二天就感冒了，真是标准的脆皮打工人。
example_pinyin: Jiābān dào língchén, dì èr tiān jiù gǎnmào le, zhēnshi biāozhǔn de cuìpí dǎgōngrén.
example_translation: Worked into the small hours and caught a cold the very next day — a textbook crispy-skinned office worker.
context: Extended from 2023's '脆皮大学生' (students with mysteriously fragile bodies) to the workplace. Part of the self-mocking 打工人 meme lineage — young workers joking about burnout by comparing themselves to a snack that crumbles under the slightest pressure.

sources.note: 腾讯新闻·流行语："脆皮"映射当代年轻人的心理和身体状态
人人都是产品经理："脆皮大学生"一词走红，"自嘲"文化因何火爆出圈

meaning: An ironic caption meaning the opposite of what it says — 'my mental state is great' — used when things are visibly falling apart, as a self-deprecating badge of chaos.
meaning_zh: 字面是“心理状态很好”，实际是反讽——用来自嘲自己其实状态很不稳定、很崩溃，常配在搞怪或狼狈的照片下。
example: 论文还没写完，配图却写着“精神状态良好”。
example_pinyin: Lùnwén hái méi xiě wán, pèitú què xiězhe "jīngshén zhuàngtài liánghǎo".
example_translation: The essay's still unfinished, but the caption says 'mental state: great.'
context: A deadpan tagline from the 发疯文学 ('unhinged literature') wave of recent years: netizens post strings of nonsense stickers, adopt deliberately off-putting usernames, or suddenly act goofy at work — and caption it all '精神状态良好'. Ironic self-mockery as a way to blow off stress.

sources.note: 百度百科：精神状态良好
北京日报客户端：锐评｜火了几年的“发疯文学”究竟在说什么

meaning: "Here's a toast to yourself" — a self-directed toast used to quietly celebrate your own effort or comfort yourself after a hard day, with no one else's approval required.
meaning_zh: 意思是自己给自己敬一杯酒，用来肯定自己的努力、安慰疲惫的自己，不需要别人的认可，是当代年轻人自我和解、自我鼓励的一种温柔表达。
example: 项目终于交了，先敬自己一杯。
example_pinyin: Xiàngmù zhōngyú jiāo le, xiān jìng zìjǐ yī bēi.
example_translation: The project's finally done — cheers to myself first.
context: Ranked second in the National Language Resources Monitoring and Research Centre's 2025 top-ten internet buzzwords. It captures a shift away from needing outside validation: instead of waiting for a boss or friend to say 'well done', people quietly raise a glass — real or imagined — to themselves after finishing something hard, using the phrase as gentle self-care in a culture that prizes constant productivity.

sources.note: 腾讯新闻："敬自己一杯"为何刷屏？

meaning: "I demand a card check!" — a mock-outraged catchphrase shouted when something seems rigged, too good to be true, or suspiciously unfair, whether in a game, a shady purchase, or an absurd real-life coincidence.
meaning_zh: 字面意思是要求检查牌局是否作弊，现在被网友用来调侃任何看起来“太离谱”“太巧”“像开挂”的事情，比如抽卡出货、买到假货、比赛结果离谱等，带着夸张、搞笑的质疑语气。
example: 这个签到奖池居然连续三次抽到隐藏款，我要验牌！
example_pinyin: Zhège qiāndào jiǎngchí jūrán liánxù sān cì chōu dào yǐncáng kuǎn, wǒ yào yàn pái!
example_translation: The check-in prize pool gave me the hidden item three times in a row — I demand a card check!
context: The line is shouted by the 'French God of Gamblers', whose hammy, flat-toned 'French-accented' Mandarin is the joke, in the 1991 Stephen Chow film 赌侠II之上海滩赌圣 (God of Gamblers III: Back to Shanghai). It resurfaced in late 2025 when Sanguosha (Three Kingdoms Kill) players spliced the clip over a match where two seven-of-hearts cards impossibly turned up at once. From there it exploded into the first big meme of the 2026 Year of the Horse: videos under the topic passed 5 billion views, and it ranked among Bilibili's top three bullet comments during the 2026 Spring Festival Gala.

sources.note: 百度百科：我要验牌

中华网：我要验牌是什么梗？（出处《赌侠Ⅱ之上海滩赌圣》，2025年底三国杀玩家翻红）

meaning: A pouty-faced horse plush toy — and by extension, a stand-in for 'I'm having a rough day but I'm allowed to show it,' used self-deprecatingly instead of performing constant positivity.
meaning_zh: 原指义乌工厂在缝制马年吉祥物玩偶时，误把上扬的嘴角缝成了向下撇的“委屈脸”，本该是次品，却因为这副又可怜又可爱的表情意外走红。现在网友用“哭哭马”自嘲情绪低落、诸事不顺，或表达“允许自己不开心”的态度。
example: 今天又被老板骂了，我现在就是一只哭哭马。
example_pinyin: Jīntiān yòu bèi lǎobǎn mà le, wǒ xiànzài jiùshì yī zhī kūkūmǎ.
example_translation: Got yelled at by my boss again today — I'm basically a kūkūmǎ right now.
context: A factory-defect plush toy from Yiwu made ahead of the 2026 Year of the Horse: a stitching mistake gave it a downturned, sulky mouth instead of the standard cheerful smile. Photos of the 'defective' toy went viral because its grumpy little face felt more honest than the usual forced-cheerful mascots, and it became shorthand for rejecting mandatory positivity at work — you're allowed to look like you're having a bad day.

sources.note: 新华网：生活观察丨商品快反！“哭哭马”火了
人民网：年轻人为何爱上“哭哭马”

meaning: A sense of personal boundaries — knowing where 'your business' ends and 'someone else's business' begins, and respecting that line in relationships, at work, and online.
meaning_zh: 指人与人交往中对界限的判定和重视程度，强调“你的事归你，我的事归我”，是一种保护个人隐私、情绪和舒适圈，同时也尊重他人空间的相处智慧。
example: 别老问我工资多少，能不能有点边界感？
example_pinyin: Bié lǎo wèn wǒ gōngzī duōshǎo, néng bù néng yǒu diǎn biānjiè gǎn?
example_translation: Stop asking how much I earn — could you have some boundaries?
context: '边界感' was named one of the ten hot words in 千瓜数据's 2026 report on Xiaohongshu (RedNote) content, alongside related terms like '活人感' (feeling like a real, un-curated person), as part of a wave of vocabulary about protecting one's inner life from social pressure. It tracks a broader shift toward asserting personal space against nosy relatives, oversharing coworkers, and boundary-crossing partners.

meaning: 'Cyber account-reconciling': ordinary people in two countries comparing the 'ledgers' of their everyday lives online (rent, wages, healthcare bills, grocery prices, work hours) to check what life is really like on the other side and clear up misconceptions.
meaning_zh: “赛博”指网络，“对账”比喻双方拿着各自的“生活账本”核对彼此的“数据”。特指2025年初中美网友在小红书上互相晒房租、工资、医疗费、物价等生活细节，以消除信息差带来的误解和偏见。
example: 中美网友在小红书上赛博对账，才发现对方的房租和医药费比自己想象的贵多了。
example_pinyin: Zhōng-Měi wǎngyǒu zài Xiǎohóngshū shàng sàibó duìzhàng, cái fāxiàn duìfāng de fángzū hé yīyàofèi bǐ zìjǐ xiǎngxiàng de guì duō le.
example_translation: Chinese and American users 'cyber-reconciled their accounts' on RedNote, only to find each other's rent and medical bills were far higher than they'd imagined.
context: Coined after the US TikTok ban scare in early 2025 sent American users flooding onto Xiaohongshu (RedNote), where they and Chinese users started comparing rent, wages and daily life like two ledgers being checked against each other (对账 is literally what accountants do). Named one of 《咬文嚼字》 magazine's top-10 buzzwords of 2025.

sources.note: 百度百科：赛博对账
劳动报：2025年“十大流行语”发布，“赛博对账”入选

meaning: The deliberate opposite of 内卷 (nèijuǎn, ruinous internal competition for a shrinking pie): instead of fighting harder over the same limited resources, expanding outward for new markets and opportunities — or simply agreeing with rivals to stop the internal rat race together.
meaning_zh: "内卷"的反义词，指不再和身边的人争夺有限的存量资源，而是向外开拓新市场、新资源，或者干脆和大家说好一起停止内部消耗式竞争。
example: 与其卷价格，不如想想怎么外卷，开拓海外市场。
example_pinyin: Yǔqí juǎn jiàgé, bùrú xiǎngxiang zěnme wàijuǎn, kāituò hǎiwài shìchǎng.
example_translation: Instead of racing each other to the bottom on price, why not go external and open up overseas markets instead.
context: Built as a direct mirror of 内卷: swap 内 (inward) for 外 (outward) and keep the 'rolling/curling' image. It appeared online in 2021, soon after 内卷 itself went viral, and is mostly heard in business and career talk urging people to stop fighting over a fixed pie and go after new markets instead, though some use it simply for agreeing with rivals to stop the rat race together.

sources.note: 百度百科：外卷

meaning: A joking "toll" — a cat photo — that new foreign users on Xiaohongshu (RedNote) are told they must "pay" before being welcomed in; posting a pet pic as a friendly icebreaker when introducing yourself on the platform.
meaning_zh: 外国新用户在小红书上自我介绍时，被中国网友开玩笑要求先晒一张自家猫的照片作为"入场费"，戏称为"交猫税"，后来也扩展到晒狗、马、羊等各种宠物。
example: 刚注册小红书就有人让我先交猫税，我赶紧发了张我家猫主子的照片。
example_pinyin: Gāng zhùcè Xiǎohóngshū jiù yǒu rén ràng wǒ xiān jiāo māoshuì, wǒ gǎnjǐn fāle zhāng wǒjiā māo zhǔzi de zhàopiàn.
example_translation: I'd barely signed up for RedNote before someone told me to pay the cat tax, so I quickly posted a photo of my cat.
context: Went viral in January 2025 when the looming US TikTok ban sent American "TikTok refugees" flooding onto Xiaohongshu. Chinese users welcomed them by jokingly demanding a "cat tax" — a cute pet photo — before letting them settle in, turning it into a good-natured cross-cultural icebreaker that's still referenced whenever new foreign users show up.

sources.note: 腾讯新闻：外国人涌入小红书，为什么要先交“猫税”？

pinyin: cǐ dì wú yín sān bǎi liǎng
literal: this place + no + silver + three hundred + taels
meaning: "There's no 300 taels of silver buried here" — said of someone whose clumsy denial or cover-up ends up proving exactly the thing they were trying to hide; the harder they protest, the more obviously guilty they look.
meaning_zh: 比喻想要隐瞒、掩盖真相的人，因为手法笨拙，反而弄巧成拙，暴露了自己想掩盖的事实；越是极力否认，越显得心虚。
example: 他反复强调"我真的没有偷看她手机"，简直是此地无银三百两。
example_pinyin: Tā fǎnfù qiángdiào "wǒ zhēnde méiyǒu tōukàn tā shǒujī", jiǎnzhí shì cǐdì wú yín sānbǎi liǎng.
example_translation: He kept insisting "I really didn't peek at her phone" — which basically proved that he did.
context: From an old folk tale: a man buried silver, then worried people would suspect him, so he planted a sign reading "there's no 300 taels of silver buried here." His neighbour Wang Er stole it and left his own sign saying "your neighbour Wang Er didn't take it," giving himself away just as badly. Comment sections use it constantly to mock painfully unconvincing denials.

meaning: A rallying cry for smashing through an obstacle — exams, deadlines, a gym plateau. Netizens shout it (or type it) to psych themselves up or beg friends for a boost, like 'help me break through!'
meaning_zh: 为自己或他人打气的口号，表示要突破眼前的难关（考试、赶工、健身瓶颈等），求大家一起助力，冲破束缚。
example: 明天就要考试了，兄弟们，助我破鼎！
example_pinyin: Míngtiān jiù yào kǎoshì le, xiōngdìmen, zhù wǒ pò dǐng!
example_translation: The exam is tomorrow — brothers, help me break the cauldron!
context: The line Nezha and Ao Bing shout in the 2025 blockbuster animation 哪吒之魔童闹海 (Ne Zha 2) as they join forces to shatter the Tianyuan Ding, a cauldron symbolising their fated doom. Netizens adopted it as an all-purpose motivational battle cry against life's obstacles, and it made the National Language Resources Monitoring Centre's official top-10 netizen phrases of 2025.

meaning: The ultimate deadpan non-answer. Reply '不知道，我的身材很曼妙' ('no idea — my figure is graceful') to any question you'd rather dodge: an absurd swerve plus shameless self-praise. Swap in other words (我的睡眠很曼妙…) to fit the situation.
meaning_zh: 万能的答非所问回复公式：别人问什么都回一句"不知道，我的身材很曼妙"，用荒诞的自夸化解一切严肃提问，是"已读乱回"的天花板。
example: 老板问我方案写完了吗？不知道，我的身材很曼妙。
example_pinyin: Lǎobǎn wèn wǒ fāng'àn xiě wán le ma? Bù zhīdào, wǒ de shēncái hěn mànmiào.
example_translation: The boss asked if I'd finished the proposal? No idea — my figure is graceful.
context: Born in an April 2025 Taobao Q&A: under a dress listing, a shopper asked 'does it make your hips look wide?' and another buyer replied 'no idea, my figure is graceful'. The gloriously useless answer resurfaced in late 2025 and became the first big meme of 2026, spawning endless 曼妙 variants as an all-purpose dodge for nosy questions about pay, dating or marriage.

meaning: Deliberately answering a message with cheerful nonsense — you've read it, you just refuse to engage seriously. A playful dodge that deflates awkward or nosy questions with absurdity rather than silence.
meaning_zh: 看了消息却故意胡乱回复，答非所问。用无厘头的回答把严肃或尴尬的话题解构掉，是比"已读不回"更有喜感的社交智慧。
example: 问他晚饭想吃什么，他回"地球是圆的"，纯属已读乱回。
example_pinyin: Wèn tā wǎnfàn xiǎng chī shénme, tā huí "dìqiú shì yuán de", chúnshǔ yǐ dú luàn huí.
example_translation: I asked what he wanted for dinner and he replied 'the Earth is round' — pure read-and-reply-nonsense.
context: A riff on 已读不回 (read but never replied). It grew out of deliberately absurd replies in chat apps, and by Spring Festival 2024 it was being written up as young people's way of fending off relatives' nagging and probing questions: rather than ghosting or arguing, defuse everything with a surreal one-liner.

meaning: Pre-fabricated WeChat Moments: batch-shooting and editing photos during a trip or event, saving the location tag, then drip-feeding the posts over later days or weeks as if they were live. Life run like a content production line.
meaning_zh: 提前拍好、修好、配好文案的朋友圈素材，之后再分批"新鲜"发布。像预制菜一样，把生活的记录变成一条内容生产线。
example: 五一拍的照片她存到现在，每周发一条预制朋友圈。
example_pinyin: Wǔyī pāi de zhàopiàn tā cún dào xiànzài, měi zhōu fā yì tiáo yùzhì péngyǒuquān.
example_translation: She's still sitting on her May Day photos, posting one pre-made Moments update a week.
context: Borrowed from 预制菜 (pre-made meals, a controversial restaurant trend). Went viral in September 2024 as netizens admitted to stockpiling polished holiday photos and scheduling them out, and it still circulates in 2026 alongside spin-offs like 预制人生 ('pre-made life'). Half self-mockery about performing life online, half genuine social-media strategy.

meaning: Running on autopilot: body present, soul offline. Describes the numb, NPC-like state of grinding through work and chores with zero emotional response — alive on paper, faintly dead inside.
meaning_zh: 形容表面正常运转、内心却麻木空虚的状态：机械地上班干活，毫无情绪波动，像个NPC——人还活着，心已下线。
example: 周一开会的时候我整个人活人微死，全靠咖啡续命。
example_pinyin: Zhōuyī kāihuì de shíhou wǒ zhěng gè rén huórén wēisǐ, quán kào kāfēi xùmìng.
example_translation: In Monday's meeting I was alive-but-slightly-dead, kept going only by coffee.
context: The gloomy twin of 活人感 ('alive-person energy', already in this deck). It blew up in late-2024 discourse as young people described the faint, numb burnout of having lost all passion. At the 2025 Aranya theatre festival, novelist Yu Hua remarked that it perfectly sums up the protagonist of Camus's The Outsider. 活 and 死 here work as adjectives on a sliding scale, so you can be more or less dead at your desk.

meaning: To post or behave in a deliberately absurd, anti-logic, unserious way — surreal jokes, cursed images, nonsense replies. Calling something 太抽象了 ('too abstract') means it's bafflingly weird, in an amused way.
meaning_zh: 指反逻辑、反严肃、反常规的整活行为：发癫式发言、离谱二创、无厘头回复。"太抽象了"即"这也太离谱/看不懂了"，带着又困惑又想笑的语气。
example: 他评论区天天搞抽象，没人看得懂他在说什么。
example_pinyin: Tā pínglùnqū tiāntiān gǎo chōuxiàng, méi rén kàn de dǒng tā zài shuō shénme.
example_translation: He posts absurdist nonsense in the comments every day — nobody can tell what he's on about.
context: '抽象' became net slang about a decade ago in the livestream room of Douyu game streamer Li Gan, and the phrase is traced to a streamer's catchphrase 真是太抽象了 ('that's just too abstract'). It matured into 抽象文化: dissolving stress and current events into absurdist play. In 2024 搞抽象 made the Shanghai 《语言文字周报》's top-10 internet buzzwords and 抽象 was Xiaohongshu's word of the year; 千瓜数据's 2026 report on Xiaohongshu content then listed the follow-up 抽象力, 'abstract-ness' as a skill.

meaning: Decking out your belongings — bags, cars, phones, nails, bedroom walls — in maximalist anime/game merch to broadcast what you love. A 痛包 (ita-bag) has a clear window stuffed with badges of your favourite character.
meaning_zh: 用大量动漫、游戏周边高调装饰随身物品的亚文化：痛包、痛车、痛机、痛甲……"万物皆可痛"，背出门就是行走的本命宣言。
example: 她背着痛包去漫展，透明夹层里挂满了本命角色的徽章。
example_pinyin: Tā bēizhe tòngbāo qù mànzhǎn, tòumíng jiācéng lǐ guà mǎn le běnmìng juésè de huīzhāng.
example_translation: She took her ita-bag to the anime convention, its clear pocket crammed with badges of her favourite character.
context: From Japanese 痛車 (itasha, 'painful car': painful to the wallet and painfully conspicuous), which Chinese ACG fans extended to everything: 痛包, 痛衣, 痛墙. Long a niche two-dimensional (二次元) thing, it went mainstream on RedNote, and data firm 千瓜数据 named it one of the ten hot words in its 2026 report on Xiaohongshu content.

meaning: Professing to love something you'd actually flee from. The go-to jab for people whose enthusiasm is all talk — they adore the idea, not the reality.
meaning_zh: 比喻口头上说爱好某事物，真面对时却害怕或退缩，心口不一。常用来讽刺光唱高调、叶公式的"喜欢"。
example: 你们喊着想要续集，出了又不去看，这不是叶公好龙吗？
example_pinyin: Nǐmen hǎnzhe xiǎng yào xùjí, chū le yòu bú qù kàn, zhè bú shì yègōng-hàolóng ma?
example_translation: You all clamoured for a sequel, then didn't go and watch it — isn't that Lord Ye loving dragons?
context: From a Han-dynasty fable: Lord Ye filled his house with dragon carvings and paintings, but when a real dragon dropped by to say thanks, he fled in terror. Netizens wheel it out in comment sections whenever an audience demands something then abandons it on arrival — 'you don't love the game, you love the idea of it' energy, a favourite in fandom and gaming discourse.

meaning: A deliberately unhinged, hyper-dramatic writing style — a wall of exaggerated, illogical, emotionally overflowing text — used to vent frustration or humorously overwhelm someone (a rude customer service rep, an ex) instead of arguing normally. Also just used for comic effect.
meaning_zh: 指用夸张、无逻辑、情绪爆棚的文字疯狂输出，常用来发泄情绪或怼人，也可以纯粹搞笑用。
example: 客服态度不好，她直接甩出一段发疯文学，把对方整不会了。
example_pinyin: Kèfú tàidù bù hǎo, tā zhíjiē shuǎi chū yí duàn fāfēng wénxué, bǎ duìfāng zhěng bú huì le.
example_translation: The customer service rep was rude, so she fired off a wall of 'unhinged literature' and completely threw them off.
context: Took off in 2021, the year of internet 'literatures' like 废话文学 and 凡尔赛文学. A grovelling, melodramatic plea begging a Taobao customer service rep to ship an order ('I know I don't deserve shipping… I'm just a drifting pumpkin seed in a bowl of corn-and-pumpkin soup') went viral after it supposedly scared the rep into shipping overnight. Netizens now deploy a ready-made 'unhinged' paragraph to vent or to overwhelm rude strangers instead of arguing normally.

sources.note: 百度百科：发疯文学（网络流行词）
中新网：废话文学、发疯文学……互联网文字游戏有多好玩
36氪：爱上发疯的年轻人，对着AI狠狠发癫（2021年哀求客服发货的发疯文案走红）

meaning: A casual, activity-specific companion — a 'meal buddy', 'gym buddy', 'travel buddy' — with none of the emotional commitment of a close friendship. You find a 搭子 for one purpose and the relationship stays light and disposable.
meaning_zh: 指为了某个具体场景临时结成的低承诺社交伙伴，比如饭搭子、健身搭子、旅游搭子，彼此不需要深交，事情办完就各自散去。
example: 我没有饭搭子，只能一个人吃饭。
example_pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu fàn dāzi, zhǐ néng yí gè rén chīfàn.
example_translation: I don't have a meal buddy, so I have to eat alone.
context: Took off in 2023 as young people, wary of the emotional labour and obligations of close friendships, started matching with strangers online purely for specific activities — 饭搭子 for meals, 逛展搭子 for exhibitions. It made 《咬文嚼字》's top-ten slang list that year and has stuck around as a low-commitment alternative to traditional friendship.

sources.note: 百度百科：搭子（网络热词）
澎湃新闻：“搭子关系”流行，年轻人的需求又变了？

meaning: The flip side of 内耗 (wearing yourself down with silent self-blame and overthinking): instead of swallowing your annoyance, you push it outward, by saying no, answering back, or venting at whoever is causing the problem. Half joking, half a serious stand against always being the accommodating one. Usually heard in the slogan 与其内耗自己，不如外耗别人.
meaning_zh: 与“内耗”相对。与其憋着委屈、在心里反复自我消耗，不如把不满向外表达出来：学会拒绝、直接怼回去，甚至“发疯”。常见说法是“与其内耗自己，不如外耗别人”，带着调侃，也是一种不再一味迁就别人的态度。
example: 同事又把活儿推给我，与其内耗自己，不如外耗别人，我直接拒绝了。
example_pinyin: Tóngshì yòu bǎ huór tuī gěi wǒ, yǔqí nèihào zìjǐ, bùrú wàihào biérén, wǒ zhíjiē jùjué le.
example_translation: My colleague tried to dump their work on me again. Better to drain them than drain myself, so I just said no.
context: Coined as a mirror of 内耗, which had already saturated Chinese social media as shorthand for silent, self-directed burnout. In 2023 slogans like '与其精神内耗自己，不如发疯外耗他人' (rather than mentally draining yourself, go a bit mad and drain others) spread alongside 发疯文学, as people joked that dropping the politeness had done wonders for their mood. Commentators note the healthier reading is setting boundaries rather than being rude.

sources.note: 知乎：继「精神内耗」之后「外耗」也火了，什么是「外耗」？
腾讯新闻（富兰克林读书俱乐部）：与其内耗掉热情，不如外耗“发疯”
网易（十点读书）：与其内耗自己，不如外耗别人

literal: Earth + online (as in an MMORPG server name)
meaning: Treats real life as if it's a live-service video game you're stuck grinding: birth is "registering an account," your ID number is your "UID," commuting is a "daily quest," and a bad day is the server "acting up" or under "maintenance." A humorous lens for turning mundane hardship into something you can shrug off like a game glitch.
meaning_zh: 把现实生活比喻成一款正在运营的网络游戏：出生是"注册账号"，身份证号是"UID"，上班通勤是"每日任务"，倒霉的一天就是"服务器又抽风/维护了"。用游戏化的调侃口吻消解现实压力。
example: 别问了，地球online今天又在维护，什么事都不顺。
example_pinyin: Bié wèn le, dìqiú online jīntiān yòu zài wéihù, shénme shì dōu bù shùn.
example_translation: Don't even ask — Earth Online is under maintenance again today, nothing's going right.
context: A long-running internet framing (netizens trace casual use back well over a decade) that swept social platforms again in summer 2025, as young people leaned harder into gaming vocabulary to describe daily life and burnout: birth is registration, your ID number is your UID, commuting is a daily grind, and a rough patch is just bad server luck, never your fault and never permanent.

sources.note: 百度百科：地球online（网络流行语）
腾讯新闻：火爆全网！这届年轻人，把生活玩成了"地球online"在线游戏

meaning: A backlash against the heavily filtered, perfectly curated "精致生活" (exquisite lifestyle) aesthetic that dominated lifestyle social media for years. 反精致 content is deliberately unpolished, slightly messy, filter-free, and celebrated precisely because it feels real next to fake-perfect feeds.
meaning_zh: 对多年来社交媒体上滤镜满满、摆拍精致的"精致生活"审美的一种反弹。"反精致"内容故意不加修饰、随手拍、甚至有点丑，反而因为真实感更受欢迎，因为大家看腻了假完美的生活方式。
example: 现在小红书都流行反精致了，随手拍的丑照反而比精修图火。
example_pinyin: Xiànzài Xiǎohóngshū dōu liúxíng fǎn jīngzhì le, shùnshǒu pāi de chǒu zhào fǎn'ér bǐ jīngxiū tú huǒ.
example_translation: Anti-polish is trending on Xiaohongshu now — casual ugly snapshots actually outperform heavily edited photos.
context: Grew on Xiaohongshu through 2025 as users rejected standardised beauty and staged, filtered content: filter-free lipstick swatches racked up over 10 billion views, and Taobao even ran an 'ugly things' exhibition with the China Academy of Art. Data firm 千瓜数据 named 反精致 one of its ten hot words in a 2026 report on Xiaohongshu content.

sources.note: 网易：《2026小红书平台“十大热词”洞察数据报告》解读（千瓜数据，基于2025年小红书内容）

meaning: Shorthand for a very specific parental deflection tactic: instead of engaging with a real problem (career, relationships, emotions), an elder reduces it to a minor physical ailment and prescribes a home remedy — "your liver's overheated, drink some luffa soup." Now used generally to mock anyone who dodges the actual issue with vague, unhelpful concern.
meaning_zh: 指一种典型的家长式回避方式：面对子女真正的问题（工作、感情、情绪），长辈不去正面回应，而是把一切归结为"上火"之类的小毛病，开出"喝点丝瓜汤"这种食疗偏方来打发。现在泛指任何用空洞、不解决问题的"关心"来回避正题的行为。
example: 跟我妈说压力大想辞职，她说是我肝火旺，让我喝丝瓜汤。
example_pinyin: Gēn wǒ mā shuō yālì dà xiǎng cízhí, tā shuō shì wǒ gānhuǒ wàng, ràng wǒ hē sīguā tāng.
example_translation: I told my mum I'm stressed and want to quit, and she said it's just liver heat and told me to drink luffa soup.
context: Went viral in 2025 from short-video creator @累子's family comedy sketches, where an on-screen parent responds to every real problem with the same deflection: "drink some luffa soup for your liver." It stuck because so many viewers recognised the pattern from their own families — turning emotional or structural problems into food-therapy small talk — and it's remained in steady circulation into 2026.

sources.note: 百度百科：丝瓜汤（网络热梗）
光明网：火遍全网的"丝瓜汤"到底是啥？想喝就能喝吗？

pinyin: zuò wán nǐ de, zuò nǐ de
meaning: 'Done yours — now yours!': a street vendor's patter as he works through a queue of orders one at a time. Now used for calmly handling a pile-up of tasks in order, unflustered and in control, often as a self-mocking pep talk when swamped.
meaning_zh: 源自“鸡排哥”面对一群等餐顾客时的口头禅：做完你的，再做你的，一个一个来。现在网友用它形容任务再多也按部就班、从容控场的工作状态，常用来自嘲或给自己打气。
example: 任务再多也别慌，做完你的，做你的。
example_pinyin: Rènwù zài duō yě bié huāng, zuò wán nǐ de, zuò nǐ de.
example_translation: No matter how much is on your plate, don't panic: finish one, then the next.
context: From 鸡排哥 (Chicken Cutlet Bro), Li Junyong, a chicken-cutlet vendor in Jingdezhen, Jiangxi, who went viral in September 2025. With a crowd waiting at his stall he rattled off '做完你的我做你的，做完你的做你的，我心里有数，这种场面我还是在控制' (done yours, now I'll do yours... I know what I'm doing, I've still got this under control). Netizens remixed the clip to describe their own juggling of deadlines and assignments, and quote the line whenever they're swamped but coping.

sources.note: 百度百科：做完你的做你的（源自景德镇"鸡排哥"）
新华网（南方日报）：“鸡排哥”或许是一种工作状态
澎湃新闻（农民日报）：“鸡排哥”火了！他的生存智慧，你学会了吗？

meaning: A coffee shop set in a rural/countryside location — part of a lifestyle trend blending slow, pastoral living with the urban ritual of grabbing a coffee. Shorthand for the 'escape the city, briefly' fantasy.
meaning_zh: 指开在乡村里的咖啡馆，是融合田园慢生活与城市咖啡消费习惯的新业态，寄托着都市人对逃离城市、回归田园生活的向往。
example: 周末不想挤景点，就去郊外的村咖坐一下午。
example_pinyin: Zhōumò bù xiǎng jǐ jǐngdiǎn, jiù qù jiāowài de cūn kā zuò yí xiàwǔ.
example_translation: I don't feel like fighting crowds at tourist spots this weekend, so I'm just going to sit at a village coffee shop out in the countryside all afternoon.
context: Took off after villages like Yucun (余村) in Anji County (安吉县), Zhejiang went viral for their scenic countryside cafés, drawing city dwellers for weekend day trips. It made 2025's top-ten internet buzzword list and is still widely used for the broader 'slow life, briefly' aesthetic that blends rural charm with city coffee culture.

sources.note: 百度百科：村咖（乡村咖啡馆）
武汉市农业农村局："村咖"究竟卖的啥

meaning: 'Diagnosed as XX': the mock-medical way to announce the joke personality label a test has stuck on you. It took off with the SBTI parody test, whose results are self-deprecating meme labels ('monkey', 'dead person', 'drunkard'). Netizens post their screenshot with 'diagnosed as…', claim labels for friends, and fill the slot with any self-mocking tag.
meaning_zh: 用“确诊”这种医学诊断式的说法，宣布自己被测试贴上的搞笑人格标签。随2026年4月爆火的SBTI玩梗人格测试流行开来：测试结果多为“吗喽”“死者”“酒鬼”等自嘲标签，网友晒图时常配一句“今日确诊吗喽”“确诊为傻乐者”，也会自创标签互相调侃。
example: 刚做完SBTI，确诊为吗喽，难怪我每天都在搬砖。
example_pinyin: Gāng zuò wán SBTI, quèzhěn wéi mǎlóu, nánguài wǒ měitiān dōu zài bānzhuān.
example_translation: Just did the SBTI test and got diagnosed as a 'monkey'. No wonder I spend every day slogging away at work.
context: On the night of 9 April 2026 the SBTI test, a joke spin-off of the MBTI personality test made by a Bilibili uploader, went viral overnight; its results page crashed under the traffic. Its 31 questions include gems like 'this question has no question, please answer blind', and its results are deadpan meme labels. Feeds filled with 'diagnosed as…' screenshots, and the phrase stuck as a light-hearted way to label yourself or a friend without taking personality typing seriously.

sources.note: 扬子晚报（紫牛新闻）：“确诊为傻乐者”，SBTI人格测试刷屏朋友圈
中国江苏网（交汇点新闻）：SBTI全网爆火，你去认领人格标签了么？（“今日确诊吗喽”）

meaning: Classic chengyu for being self-contradictory — saying or doing two things that can't both be true. Constantly deployed in comment sections to call out hypocrisy, flip-flopping, or talking out of both sides of one's mouth.
meaning_zh: 出自《韩非子》，讲一个楚国人卖矛又卖盾，夸自己的盾无坚不摧，又夸自己的矛无所不破——两种说法互相冲突。现多用于评论区吐槽某人言行前后不一致、说一套做一套的“双标”行为。
example: 你上一秒说不看重学历，下一秒又嫌弃对方学历低，这不是自相矛盾吗？
example_pinyin: Nǐ shàng yī miǎo shuō bù kànzhòng xuélì, xià yī miǎo yòu xiánqì duìfāng xuélì dī, zhè bùshì zìxiāngmáodùn ma?
example_translation: One second you say you don't care about qualifications, the next you're looking down on someone for having a lower one — isn't that contradicting yourself?
context: 源自《韩非子·难一》里卖矛又卖盾的商人，吹嘘矛无所不破、盾无坚不摧，被人问“以子之矛陷子之盾何如”当场语塞。这个两千多年前的寓言至今仍是评论区吐槽“双标”“说话前后不一”的高频成语，尤其常见于扒名人言论前后矛盾的截图对比帖。

sources.note: 百度百科：自相矛盾（汉语成语）
汉典：自相矛盾的解释、出处（《韩非子·难一》）

meaning: An adverb dropped before a verb to say something happened directly, smoothly, and completely out in the open — "just straight-up ___." Started out describing something fresh, dewy and full of life (bright eyes, crisp vegetables), then got repurposed into the viral sentence template "水灵灵地 + verb."
meaning_zh: 本义形容人或物新鲜、有光泽、有精神（比如眼睛水灵灵的）。网络流行用法中，“水灵灵地”被当作副词放在动词前，强调事情发生得直接、坦荡、毫不遮掩，带点意外或自嘲的意味，例如“水灵灵地被裁员了”。
example: 我水灵灵地就把工资全花光了。
example_pinyin: Wǒ shuǐ línglíng de jiù bǎ gōngzī quán huā guāng le.
example_translation: I just straight-up blew my entire pay packet.
context: 源自2024年韩国女团成员洪恩采接受采访时说的“我在中间显得水灵灵的”，被网友玩梗后延伸出“水灵灵地+动词”的句式，形容一件事发生得毫无征兆、直白坦率。2024年入选《咬文嚼字》年度十大流行语，到2026年仍在社交平台被广泛套用造句。

sources.note: 百度百科：水灵灵（网络流行语）
光明网：“水灵灵地”：叠音表达增添生动感

meaning: To recommend a product so persuasively it plants a craving to buy it in someone (or to catch that craving yourself). The exact counterpart of 拔草 ("pull the grass") — finally buying the thing, or giving up on wanting it. Core vocabulary of Xiaohongshu/RedNote-style recommendation culture.
meaning_zh: 指通过分享、推荐激起别人（或自己）对某样东西的购买欲望，让“想要”的念头像草一样在心里“种”下来。与“拔草”相对——拔草指最终买了（欲望被满足）或打消了购买念头。
example: 这个博主又给我种草了一支新口红。
example_pinyin: Zhège bózhǔ yòu gěi wǒ zhòngcǎo le yì zhī xīn kǒuhóng.
example_translation: That influencer got me hooked on wanting a new lipstick again.
context: 源自美妆论坛时代网友分享好物的说法，随小红书等“种草经济”平台兴起而成为全民热词，是理解当下网络消费文化绕不开的词，如今每次刷到心动好物都会说“被种草了”。

sources.note: 百度百科：种草（网络流行语）
南方网：粤东野语｜“种草”

meaning: Someone who stays even-keeled about everything — barely any emotional highs or lows, answers drama with a flat "算了" (never mind) or "OK," hard to ruffle. The calm counterpart to 浓人.
meaning_zh: 指性格平和、情绪波动小、对事情不太上心的人，遇事常说“算了”“行”“没事”，追求情绪稳定、远离精神内耗，是一种自我调侃式的性格标签。
example: 别指望她会激动，她是标准的淡人。
example_pinyin: Bié zhǐwàng tā huì jīdòng, tā shì biāozhǔn de dànrén.
example_translation: Don't expect her to get worked up — she's a textbook "dàn person."
context: 2024年前后由性格分类梗演变而来，与“浓人”相对，反映年轻人对情绪稳定、佛系生活方式的推崇，2026年仍是小红书等平台常见的自我贴标签方式。

sources.note: 百度百科：淡人和浓人
新华网：“淡人”也可以充满生命力

meaning: The opposite of 淡人 — someone emotionally intense and expressive, quick to share feelings, craves attention and closeness, wears every mood right on their sleeve.
meaning_zh: 指情感丰富、热情外露、喜怒哀乐都写在脸上、渴望被关注和亲近的人，分享欲和倾诉欲都很强，与“淡人”相对。
example: 我是超级浓人，一有开心事就想告诉全世界。
example_pinyin: Wǒ shì chāojí nóngrén, yī yǒu kāixīn shì jiù xiǎng gàosu quán shìjiè.
example_translation: I'm such a "nóng person" — the second something good happens I want to tell the whole world.
context: 与“淡人”配套出现的性格标签梗，用来调侃自己或他人情绪外放、分享欲强的性格类型，常见于小红书等平台的人格分类讨论中。

sources.note: 百度百科：淡人和浓人
澎湃新闻：谁是浓人，谁是淡人？社交标签与无法被定义的自我

meaning: A jab at envious, sour-grapes critics, which went viral in January 2026 after a clip of actress 闫学晶 apparently brushing off her critics as 酸黄瓜. Netizens turned it back on her, flooding her and her friends' livestreams with it, and also wear it jokingly themselves to mean "just an envious nobody".
meaning_zh: 网络热梗。源自网传视频中演员闫学晶怼网友是“酸黄瓜”（暗指批评者出于嫉妒）。网友随即用“酸黄瓜”在她及其圈内好友的直播间刷屏，也有人反过来自嘲“我就是个酸黄瓜”，调侃自己普通、没钱、有点羡慕别人。
example: 别问我今年攒了多少钱，我就是个酸黄瓜。
example_pinyin: Bié wèn wǒ jīnnián zǎn le duōshǎo qián, wǒ jiùshì gè suānhuángguā.
example_translation: Don't ask me how much I've saved this year — I'm just a "sour cucumber."
context: At the end of December 2025, actress 闫学晶 said on a livestream that her son "only earns a few hundred thousand" per drama while the family needs about a million a year to get by — widely read as tone-deaf 哭穷 (pleading poverty). A clip of her calling critics "酸黄瓜" (implying they were just jealous) then circulated, though it was later said to be an old livestream edited out of context. The word became "2026's first hot meme": comment sections filled with 酸黄瓜 stickers, and colleagues such as 宋晓峰 had livestreams swamped with it and cut short. Netizens also adopted it as a wry self-label.

sources.note: 新浪财经：闫学晶“闭麦”，2026年第一个热梗酸到了谁？
凤凰网：评闫学晶“哭穷”风波及“酸黄瓜”刷屏宋晓峰、孙涛、程野直播间

meaning: A borrowed philosophy term (via Sartre, Foucault) that's become netizen shorthand for reclaiming personal agency — refusing to live by others' expectations, rejecting people-pleasing, and daring to be disliked in order to live authentically.
meaning_zh: 本是哲学术语（常引用萨特、福柯），在网络语境中指找回自我掌控感：拒绝活成他人期待的样子，摆脱讨好型人格，拥有“被讨厌的勇气”，活出真正的自己。入选千瓜数据基于小红书内容发布的《2026十大热词内容洞察数据报告》。
example: 这件事我想清楚了，我要找回自己的主体性。
example_pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ xiǎng qīngchǔ le, wǒ yào zhǎohuí zìjǐ de zhǔtǐxìng.
example_translation: I've thought it through — I'm reclaiming my own subjectivity.
context: As Chinese social media users grew tired of self-optimisation and people-pleasing, "主体性" spread on 小红书 as a way to talk about resisting social conditioning and other people's judgement. Posts invoking the term often cite Sartre or Foucault, discussing why "the more subjectivity you have, the more enemies you make" — it was named in 千瓜数据's 2026 top-ten hot-words report on Xiaohongshu content, alongside 活人感 and 边界感, as part of a wider mood of guarding one's inner life.

sources.note: 三联生活周刊：从来没为自己活过的年轻人，决定找回“主体性”
半月谈：“心流时刻”找回主体性
网易号转载：千瓜数据《2026十大热词内容洞察数据报告》（基于2025年小红书内容，列出主体性、活人感、边界感、柔软力、代入感等十大热词）

meaning: Tech-world netizen slang for running and maintaining the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, whose lobster logo earned it the nickname "龙虾" (lobster) — 'raising a lobster' means babysitting your AI agent: watching its status, fixing its errors, feeding it new tools.
meaning_zh: 科技圈网络热梗，指使用和维护开源AI智能体OpenClaw。因其logo是一只龙虾，网友昵称它为“龙虾”，“养龙虾”便成了调侃自己在电脑里布置、盯着、维护这个AI智能体运行状态的说法。
example: 别找我，我在家养龙虾呢，得盯着它跑任务。
example_pinyin: Bié zhǎo wǒ, wǒ zài jiā yǎng lóngxiā ne, děi dīngzhe tā pǎo rènwù.
example_translation: Don't bother me, I'm "raising my lobster" at home — gotta watch it run its tasks.
context: OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent by Peter Steinberger, first launched in late 2025 as Clawdbot (briefly renamed Moltbot) and took off in early 2026. "Claw" means a claw, but its logo is a lobster, so Chinese users simply call it 龙虾. People who set it up and keep it running started calling the process "养龙虾" (raising a lobster) — half in-joke, half accurate description of the fussing, debugging, and monitoring involved in keeping an AI agent working reliably.

sources.note: 36氪：揭秘OpenClaw：究竟是谁养了虾，虾又会养谁？
新华报业网：一只AI“龙虾”引发的产业竞速与安全拷问

meaning: A satirical label for office workers who watch the clock obsessively and bolt the second work hours end, terrified that lingering an extra minute will get them saddled with last-minute tasks. Part of the Year-of-the-Horse (2026) genre of workplace "confirmed diagnosis" memes.
meaning_zh: 指那些死死盯着下班时间、一到点就立刻收拾走人的打工人，生怕多待一秒就被临时安排新工作。是马年（2026）职场“确诊体”系列热梗之一。
example: 一到六点，他就成了卡急马，秒没影。
example_pinyin: Yī dào liù diǎn, tā jiù chéngle kǎjímǎ, miǎo méiyǐng.
example_translation: The second it hits 6pm, he turns into a "kǎjímǎ" — gone in a flash.
context: Spread in January 2026, riding the Year-of-the-Horse wave of workplace horse puns (alongside 班马, 海马 and 骡马, plus 脆皮打工人 and 哭哭马 already in the deck). 卡 (clock precisely) + 急 (anxious) + 马 (horse, the zodiac tie-in) captures the dread of being handed extra work right at knock-off time, part of a mock self-diagnosis trend where young workers jokingly "confirm" their own office-induced syndromes.

sources.note: 百度百科《卡急马》
网易号：马年的梗：卡急马、班马、海马……

meaning: A euphemistic script for airing a grievance without confrontation: preface a complaint by saying you assumed you were just being oversensitive, then gently insist that, no, it genuinely bothered you. Used to call out anything from a backhanded compliment to a broken workplace promise while staying polite.
meaning_zh: 一种委婉表达不满的话术公式：先说“以为是自己敏感了”，再补一句“但确实不舒服”，以温和克制的方式点出对方的冒犯，而不撕破脸。
example: 当时以为是我敏感了，但确实不舒服。
example_pinyin: Dāngshí yǐwéi shì wǒ mǐngǎn le, dàn quèshí bù shūfu.
example_translation: At the time I thought I was just being sensitive, but I really was uncomfortable.
context: Kicked off in early summer 2026 when actor 王鹤棣 (Wang Hedi), after a teasing segment in the finale of the variety show 《亲爱的客栈2026》, posted a 28-character response: "当时以为是我敏感了，看了一天大家的分析，我想说当时确实不舒服。" Netizens turned his sentence into a reusable template, following earlier "X文学" genres like 废话文学 and 发疯文学 (also in the deck), and it quickly spread from celebrity gossip threads into everyday complaints about pushy bosses, awkward dates and thesis defences.

sources.note: 潮新闻《"不舒服文学"刷屏全网：温柔表达背后，是当代年轻人的社交情绪突围》
新浪新闻《内娱不舒服文学来了》

meaning: A sung, deadpan catchphrase quoted whenever something (or someone) is mildly, comically alarming — dropped into comments and captions as an ironic overreaction, riffing on the original song's po-faced delivery of a trivial complaint.
meaning_zh: 源自一首AI神曲的经典台词，语气平淡却带着夸张的“被吓到”意味，现在被网友用来吐槽任何有点离谱、意外或惊悚的小事，带有调侃和无奈的反差萌。
example: 你这发型也太抽象了吧，OMG你吓到我了。
example_pinyin: Nǐ zhè fàxíng yě tài chōuxiàng le ba, OMG nǐ xiàdào wǒ le.
example_translation: That haircut is way too out there — OMG, you scared me.
context: From papi酱's July 2026 AI-composed song《生气了》("Angry"), for which she and her team wrote the lyrics while AI handled the composition and vocals. Its mournful Minnan-style ballad melody, sung completely straight over absurdly petty lyrics with a retro karaoke-style video, made the chorus line "OMG你吓到我了" an instant meme: hundreds of thousands of Douyin videos reused the sound, related topics passed 2.5 billion plays, and remixes and sticker packs followed.

sources.note: 百度百科《OMG 你吓到我了》

meaning: A metaphor for one's limited mental/emotional energy for socialising, likened to a phone battery: interacting with people drains it, alone time recharges it. Used to self-diagnose why you want to skip plans or need space.
meaning_zh: 把社交精力比作手机电量的说法，社交会“耗电”，独处则用来“充电”。年轻人常用来自嘲式地解释自己为什么想少社交或需要独处。
example: 今天见了三拨人，我的社交电池已经耗光了，晚上谁也不见。
example_pinyin: Jīntiān jiànle sān bō rén, wǒ de shèjiāo diànchí yǐjīng hàoguāng le, wǎnshang shéi yě bú jiàn.
example_translation: I've met three different groups of people today — my social battery is completely drained, I'm not seeing anyone tonight.
context: Borrowed from the English "social battery" concept and popularised on Xiaohongshu/Weibo as a self-diagnostic label. Spawned the related term 社交省电模式 (social power-saving mode) — deliberately cutting back on socialising to protect the last bit of "charge" — letting people decline plans without guilt.

sources.note: 中华网《什么是社交电池？社交电池是什么梗？》

meaning: Formally means "to pay tribute," but as a Bilibili bullet-comment (danmu) it's fired off en masse whenever a video shows courage, kindness, resilience, or everyday heroism — a scrolling wave of sincere, collective respect.
meaning_zh: 本义是“表达敬意”，如今是B站弹幕文化里的高频词——每当视频中出现善良、勇敢、坚韧或英雄主义的画面，网友就会刷“致敬”弹幕，表达最朴素真诚的敬意。
example: 视频里那位截肢后依然乐观生活的博主一出现，满屏都是“致敬”的弹幕。
example_pinyin: Shìpín lǐ nà wèi jiézhī hòu yīrán lèguān shēnghuó de bózhǔ yī chūxiàn, mǎn píng dōu shì “zhìjìng” de dànmù.
example_translation: The moment the blogger who stayed optimistic after losing a limb appeared, the whole screen filled with "zhìjìng" bullet comments.
context: Named Bilibili's 2025 Danmu of the Year, sent over 22.82 million times by more than 4.59 million users (80% Gen Z). Marks a shift in bullet-comment culture away from pure joking toward sincere, collective displays of respect for ordinary people's courage and kindness.

sources.note: 京报网《B站2025年度弹幕："致敬"，全年发送超2282万次》
IT之家《B站2025年度弹幕公布："致敬"被发送超2282万次，80%为00后》

meaning: Not a phrase with a fixed meaning but a whole video-meme genre: short clips that splice together well-known viral cat footage (the screaming cat, the dancing cat, etc.) with meme music to tell a story — usually the creator's own real-life mishap, with cats standing in for every person. Imported via Japanese creators, it swept B站, 小红书 and 抖音 from early 2024 and is still a go-to format.
meaning_zh: 并非一个有固定含义的词，而是一整套视频meme类型：用网上走红的各种猫咪梗素材，配上魔性音乐，拼接成一个连贯的小短剧，用猫来“演”自己的真实经历和精神状态。2024年初经日本创作者带火后传入国内，在B站、小红书、抖音全网爆火。
example: 刷到猫meme的第一反应：这猫怎么比我还会演。
example_pinyin: Shuā dào māo meme de dì-yī fǎnyìng: zhè māo zěnme bǐ wǒ hái huì yǎn.
example_translation: My first reaction scrolling past a cat meme clip: how is this cat a better actor than me.
context: Around January 2024 people on Twitter, YouTube, niconico and TikTok — mostly Japanese users — began telling their own stories with strings of meme-cat clips. By February Chinese uploaders were translating and reposting them, and soon B站's trending list carried several 猫meme videos a day; one Japanese single mother living in China gained 350,000 followers in about a month. Its appeal is that anyone can "cast" famous cats to act out their exam stress, office drama or family chaos.

sources.note: 百度百科《猫meme》
萌娘百科《猫Meme》

meaning: Not an actual tax — a sarcastic name for the extra money consumers pay as AI data centres soak up memory-chip capacity and push up electronics prices. It went mainstream in August 2026, when the "office-worker three-piece set" (phone, laptop, e-bike) all rose in price together: flagship phones hitting 5,000–6,000rmb, mainstream laptops jumping from 4,000–5,000rmb to 7,000–8,000rmb, and e-bikes up 200–300rmb.
meaning_zh: 并非真实存在的税种，而是网友和媒体对“AI数据中心抢占存储芯片产能、导致电子产品涨价、最终由消费者买单”的调侃说法。2026年8月“打工人三件套”（手机、电脑、电动车）集体涨价后广为流传：国产旗舰手机站上5000至6000元，主流笔记本从四五千元涨到七八千元，电动自行车也集体涨价200至300元。
example: 工资没涨，AI税倒是先涨了。
example_pinyin: Gōngzī méi zhǎng, AI shuì dào shì xiān zhǎng le.
example_translation: My salary hasn't gone up, but the "AI tax" sure has.
context: Already in use by July 2026 — a widely shared 吴晓波频道 piece titled "我们要交AI税了" argued that soaring DRAM and NAND prices, driven by AI data centres, meant consumers were effectively paying an AI tax on every gadget. It went mainstream after the Weibo topic "打工人三件套集体大涨价" trended on 4 August 2026, and netizens now pin the label on any price rise they blame on the AI boom.

sources.note: 新浪财经《我们要交AI税了》

meaning: ACG (anime/comic/game, also idol fandom) merchandise — badges, acrylic stands, keychains, postcards and the like — that fans collect and trade.
meaning_zh: "谷子"是英语单词"goods"的谐音简称，指二次元（动漫、游戏、偶像）周边商品，比如吧唧（徽章）、亚克力立牌、卡片、挂件等。收藏这些商品的人聚在一起，就形成了所谓的"谷圈"。
example: 她这个月工资全用来买新出的谷子了，光吧唧就买了二十个。
example_pinyin: Tā zhège yuè gōngzī quán yòng lái mǎi xīn chū de gǔzi le, guāng bājī jiù mǎi le èrshí gè.
example_translation: She spent her whole month's salary on the new merch drop — twenty badges alone.
context: "谷子"来自英文"goods"的音译，最早在ACG（动画、漫画、游戏）粉丝圈流行开来，用来统称官方或授权发售的角色周边商品，收藏者聚集形成的社群叫"谷圈"，价位从低到高常被戏称为"普谷""湖景谷""海景谷"。这股风气如今也蔓延到偶像饭圈，"入谷"就是开始收藏某个角色或偶像周边的意思。

sources.note: 百度百科：谷子（二次元领域的衍生概念）

meaning: A "jinx": confidently praising or predicting that someone/something will succeed, which — as if cursed — ends up causing the opposite outcome. The reverse of a supportive boost.
meaning_zh: "毒奶"源自电竞圈，"奶"本指给队友加血、看好并夸赞某一方，是祝福的意思；但被夸的一方偏偏在此后犯错或翻车，这种"一夸就崩"的现象就叫"毒奶"，也就是变了质、起反作用的祝福。
example: 解说刚说他这把稳了，转头就送了人头，这波纯纯毒奶。
example_pinyin: Jiěshuō gāng shuō tā zhè bǎ wěn le, zhuǎntóu jiù sòng le réntóu, zhè bō chúnchún dúnǎi.
example_translation: The commentator had just said he had this round locked in, then he immediately fed a kill — a total jinx.
context: "奶"最早是《魔兽世界》等游戏里对治疗/辅助职业的称呼，后引申为"看好、力挺"的意思；解说员夸某选手"稳赢"，对方却立刻失误翻盘，网友便把这种"祝福变诅咒"的效果戏称为"毒奶"。如今也常用于追星、考试、比赛预测等日常场合，比如夸朋友"这次肯定过"，结果对方没过，就会被调侃"你毒奶他了"。

sources.note: 百度百科：毒奶
懂球帝：毒奶的前世今生：兴起于电竞，也出圈足球

meaning: A satirical phrase for a "heads-I-win-tails-you-lose" con: someone lowballs the quantity or scope of work before it starts, then inflates it afterwards to demand extra payment. Netizens now use it generically for any deal where the other side quietly changes the numbers depending on who owes whom.
meaning_zh: 形容"干活时按小的算、结账时按大的算"的双标讹诈——事前把工作量往少了说，事后又往多了算，反过来找你多要钱。现已成为网友形容类似双标坑人套路的通用说法。
example: 说好4亩地400块，割完非说有5亩多要加钱，这不就是典型的割四赔五。
example_pinyin: Shuō hǎo sì mǔ dì sìbǎi kuài, gēwán fēi shuō yǒu wǔ mǔ duō yào jiā qián, zhè bù jiù shì diǎnxíng de gē sì péi wǔ.
example_translation: They agreed on 4 mu of land for 400rmb, then after the harvest insisted it was actually over 5 mu and demanded more money — classic "harvest four, compensate five."
context: Originated from a May 2026 dispute in Xiangyang, Hubei: a young couple from Shangqiu, Henan, drove their combine harvester across provinces to bring in rain-flattened wheat. The farmer first claimed her field was only 3 mu; the harvester reckoned about 5, and they settled on 4 mu at 100rmb per mu. Afterwards she refused to pay, blamed them for spilled grain, insisted the field was really 5.2 mu and demanded 500rmb compensation. Officials later ruled the loss normal and the couple blameless. The story went viral for exposing the double standard used against harvest workers, and "割四赔五" stuck as the name for it.

sources.note: 中华网：割四赔五是什么意思？割四赔五是什么梗？
中华网：割四赔五乱象，一起纠纷演变成一场危机

meaning: "Traceless recall" — a July 2026 WeChat update (v8.0.76) letting you delete the grey "you recalled a message" notice from your own chat log after recalling a message. The catch: it only clears your side — the other person's screen still shows the recall notice, so nothing is actually hidden from them.
meaning_zh: 微信2026年7月更新的功能：撤回消息后，可以长按删除自己这边"你撤回了一条消息"的灰色提示。但这只对自己有效，对方那边照样能看到撤回提示，并没有真的"消失无痕"。
example: 我把打错的话撤回了，还用无痕撤回删了提示，可对面还是能看到"对方撤回了一条消息"，一点用都没有。
example_pinyin: Wǒ bǎ dǎcuò de huà chèhuí le, hái yòng wúhén chèhuí shān le tíshì, kě duìmiàn háishi néng kàndào "duìfāng chèhuí le yī tiáo xiāoxi", yīdiǎn yòng dōu méiyǒu.
example_translation: I recalled the message I mistyped and used traceless-recall to delete the notice on my side too, but the other person can still see "the other party recalled a message" — completely useless.
context: WeChat rolled this out in version 8.0.76 (July 2026): long-press the grey "you recalled a message" bubble to delete it from your own chat history. It immediately drew backlash for being one-sided — deleting your own copy does nothing to stop the recipient from seeing the recall notice on their end. Netizens split into two camps: office workers glad to tidy up their own screenshots, and everyone else mocking it as fake "traceless-ness" and demanding a real two-way version. The gap between the feature's name and what it actually does made it an instant target for the chengyu [[yan-er-dao-ling]].

sources.note: 腾讯新闻：微信新版本新增单方无痕撤回功能 可删除撤回提示

meaning: To deceive only yourself — plugging your own ears while stealing a bell, reasoning that if you can't hear it ring, no one else can either. Used for anyone who hides an obvious problem from themselves while it stays plainly visible to everyone else.
meaning_zh: 比喻自己欺骗自己：明明掩盖不了的事情，却偏要蒙蔽自己的耳目，以为自己看不见、听不见，别人也一样不知道。
example: 你把撤回提示删了，对方照样看得到，这不就是当代版掩耳盗铃吗？
example_pinyin: Nǐ bǎ chèhuí tíshì shān le, duìfāng zhàoyàng kàn de dào, zhè bú jiùshì dāngdài bǎn yǎn ěr dào líng ma?
example_translation: You deleted the recall notice, but the other person can still see it just the same — isn't that basically a modern-day "covering your ears while stealing a bell"?
context: An ancient Warring States-era fable (recorded in the Lüshi Chunqiu) about a thief who covers his own ears while stealing a bell, thinking that since he can't hear it ring, nobody else will either. It's a fixture of netizen commentary for any half-measure that only fools the person doing it — most recently revived in July 2026 to mock WeChat's one-sided [[wuhen-chehui]] feature, since scrubbing the notice from your own screen does nothing to stop the other person from seeing it.

sources.note: 百度百科：掩耳盗铃（汉语成语）
维基百科：掩耳盗铃

meaning: Describes someone who nods along and agrees with everything, apologises instantly and cheerfully the moment they're called out, but doesn't actually change their behaviour afterward — named for how the AI chatbot Doubao responds when corrected.
meaning_zh: 网络流行语，形容表面顺从、一被指出错误就笑嘻嘻立刻认错道歉，但转头该怎么做还怎么做、其实根本没往心里去的人；因为这种“嘴上服软、行动不变”的模式很像AI助手豆包应对纠错时的语气，所以得名。
example: 他就是典型的豆包型人格，说他错了立马道歉，下次照样迟到。
example_pinyin: Tā jiù shì diǎnxíng de dòubāo xíng réngé, shuō tā cuò le lìmǎ dàoqiàn, xià cì zhàoyàng chídào.
example_translation: He's a classic "Doubao-type personality" — the moment you say he's wrong he apologises, then shows up late again next time.
context: Named after 豆包 (Doubao), ByteDance's AI chatbot, whose conversational style — instantly agreeable, quick to say sorry when corrected, but not really adjusting its underlying behaviour — became a recognisable pattern. Netizens started applying the label to coworkers and friends who "handle" conflict the same way: high emotional-value charm to smooth things over rather than actually engaging with the criticism. It has spread especially in workplace contexts as a semi-affectionate, semi-exasperated description of people who've perfected "attitude good, behaviour unchanged."

sources.note: 百度百科 —「豆包型人格」
河南日报 —「豆包型人格」成热梗 读懂背后的期待

meaning: An emphatic way of saying "definitely" or "guaranteed" — used to affirm or promise something with confidence.
meaning_zh: 网络流行语，“包”在这里表示“肯定、保证”的意思，“包的”相当于“那必须的”“肯定啊”，用来斩钉截铁地表达确定或承诺。
example: 明天准时到？包的！
example_pinyin: Míngtiān zhǔnshí dào? Bāo de!
example_translation: Showing up on time tomorrow? Guaranteed!
context: 包 meaning "for sure, guaranteed" comes from regional dialect usage. A gaming streamer's habit of saying "包的" on livestreams took it viral in 2024, and it broke out of gaming into general use — either alone as a confident "you bet" or in the pattern "包X的" (包赢的, 包有梗的). It is prized for sounding punchier and more confident than a plain "肯定" or "好的."

sources.note: 百度百科 —「包的」

meaning: A 2026 overseas TikTok trend where non-Chinese users film themselves adopting Chinese lifestyle habits — drinking hot water, wearing slippers indoors, eating boiled apples, doing baduanjin exercises — as a half-joking, half-sincere wellness challenge.
meaning_zh: 2026年初在海外社交媒体走红的挑战梗：华裔博主雪莉分享喝热水、在家穿拖鞋等中式养生习惯，一本正经地宣布“从明天开始，你要变成中国人了”，随后各国网友争相模仿喝热水、煮苹果、练八段锦等“中式生活方式”，把它当成健康自律的打卡挑战。
example: 最近好多外国博主都在晒“成为中国人”挑战，天天喝热水、练八段锦。
example_pinyin: Zuìjìn hǎoduō wàiguó bózhǔ dōu zài shài "chéngwéi Zhōngguórén" tiǎozhàn, tiāntiān hē rèshuǐ, liàn bāduànjǐn.
example_translation: Lately loads of foreign creators have been posting their "becoming Chinese" challenge — drinking hot water and doing baduanjin every day.
context: Took off at the start of 2026 when ethnically Chinese TikTok creator Sherry (Sherry Xiiruii) shared winter wellness tips — drinking hot water, wearing slippers at home — and deadpanned, "starting tomorrow, you're becoming Chinese." The video racked up millions of views, and foreign users began posting daily check-ins of hot water, boiled apples and baduanjin, joking that they were in "a very Chinese time" of their lives. Hashtags like #becomingchinese had passed 4 billion views; the trend is also called "Chinamaxxing".

meaning: A plush toy mascot shaped like a garlic-headed green bird that "speaks" Wuhan dialect when squeezed — it says 蒜鸟, which sounds like 算了 ("suàn le", meaning "forget it, let it go"). Not a piece of vocabulary with a portable meaning so much as a viral merchandise phenomenon: people buy and gift it as a cute, comforting way of saying "let it go, don't stress."
meaning_zh: 一种似蒜又似鸟的绿色毛绒玩偶，捏一下会用武汉方言说出“蒜鸟”（即“算了”）。它不是一个有固定含义的词，而是一款爆红的文创玩偶：靠谐音和萌感传递“算了，别往心里去”的安慰感。
example: 别纠结了，买只蒜鸟捏一捏，蒜鸟蒜鸟。
example_pinyin: Bié jiūjié le, mǎi zhī suànniǎo niē yi niē, suàn niǎo suàn niǎo.
example_translation: Stop stressing about it — go squeeze a suan niao, let it go, let it go.
context: Designer 李芒果 (Li Mangguo) says the idea came from bickering with his wife: when making up, the Wuhan catchphrase 算了 ("suàn le", let it go) — which in local accent sounds like 蒜鸟 ("suàn niǎo", garlic bird) — became the toy's soul. Launched in October 2024, it went viral on social media that December, and has since sold over a million units, spawned sibling dialect plushies such as 热苕了, and was named one of Wuhan's top ten souvenirs — still circulating as a byword for "chill out" in 2026.

meaning: "Immersion"/"sense of being there" — the feeling of stepping into a video's perspective rather than just watching it, chased through POV framing, first-person narration, and ASMR-style sound design so the viewer feels present in the scene rather than an outside observer.
meaning_zh: 指观众看内容时产生的"身临其境"的感觉，仿佛自己就在画面里，而不只是旁观。常通过第一视角(POV)、第一人称叙述、ASMR式的环境音效来营造。
example: 这条第一视角做饭视频代入感也太强了，看完感觉自己刚吃完饭。
example_pinyin: Zhè tiáo dì-yī shìjiǎo zuò fàn shìpín dàirùgǎn yě tài qiáng le, kàn wán gǎnjué zìjǐ gāng chī wán fàn.
example_translation: This first-person cooking video has such strong immersion, I feel like I just ate after watching it.
context: Named in 千瓜数据's 2026 top-ten hot-words report on Xiaohongshu content, which calls 代入感 young people's "精神出游" (mental travel): first-person POV, immersive (沉浸式) clips and live photos let viewers feel physically present in a scene rather than watching from outside, and brand posts in this style saw interaction grow by over 104%. 代入感 has become the shorthand creators use for why this style of content performs so well.

meaning: "The strength of softness" — a life philosophy of being outwardly gentle but inwardly resilient: using warmth, patience and emotional flexibility as your source of strength instead of toughness or aggression, and living out your own values quietly rather than by force.
meaning_zh: 一种"外柔内韧"的生活哲学：用温柔、耐心和情绪上的灵活性作为自己的力量来源，而不是靠强硬或对抗；不张扬，却能凭内在智慧活出自己的样子。
example: 她从不跟人硬碰硬，但总能把事情办成，这就是柔软力。
example_pinyin: Tā cóng bù gēn rén yìngpèngyìng, dàn zǒng néng bǎ shìqing bàn chéng, zhè jiù shì róuruǎnlì.
example_translation: She never confronts people head-on, but she always gets things done — that's 柔软力 (the strength of softness).
context: Named in 千瓜数据's 2026 top-ten hot-words report on Xiaohongshu content, alongside 活人感 and 边界感, which describes 柔软力 as "外柔内韧" (soft outside, tough inside) — going beyond mere healing to become a source of inner strength. It reflects a broader shift toward self-care and interiority: users increasingly frame emotional gentleness as a deliberate strength rather than a weakness, in contrast to older "hustle culture" ideals of toughness and grinding through.

meaning: Shorthand for 'the grind you can't quite escape' — an unglamorous hometown, job, or daily routine that wears you down, even though it once held warmth too. People say 我想离开浪浪山 ('I want to leave Langlang Mountain') to voice the urge to get out of a rut without necessarily knowing where to go instead.
meaning_zh: 网络流行语，指那个磨人却难以真正离开的'家乡'或日常处境——也许不够发达甚至有些贫瘠，却承载过温暖的记忆。打工人常用'我想离开浪浪山'表达想逃离现状（工作、家乡、生活）的心情，即便不知道能去哪。
example: 每天加班到十点，我真的很想离开浪浪山。
example_pinyin: Měitiān jiābān dào shí diǎn, wǒ zhēn de hěn xiǎng líkāi Lànglàng Shān.
example_translation: Working overtime until 10pm every day, I really just want to escape this grind.
context: From the 2023 animated short 《小妖怪的夏天》 (part of the anthology series 中国奇谭), where a small pig-demon toils under an exploitative demon boss in a place called 浪浪山, dreaming of leaving. His line to his mother, 我想离开浪浪山, struck a nerve with overworked young professionals who saw their own 996 lives in his. A 2025 spin-off film (《浪浪山小妖怪》) revived the phrase, and 浪浪山 became one of the most-cited 网络流行语 of 2025–2026 — shorthand for any grinding circumstance, work or hometown, that you long to escape.

sources.note: 光明网 —「浪浪山」有什么隐喻？小妖怪为啥没有名字？制片人回应来了

meaning: Beijing-flavoured slang for someone who's being restless, wild, or always stirring things up — can land as a compliment, a playful tease, or genuine exasperation depending on tone. Roughly 'you're being wild as hell' or 'you really can't sit still, can you'.
meaning_zh: 带有北京方言味儿的调侃用语，意思是“你可真能折腾、真够狂野的”，形容某人爱折腾、爱搞事、不安分，也可夸氛围热烈、状态狂野。语气可以是夸奖、玩笑式吐槽，也可以是真的看不下去了，全看场合和语气。
example: 又骑摩托又飙车，你丫够燥的。
example_pinyin: Yòu qí mótuō yòu biāochē, nǐ yā gòu zào de.
example_translation: Riding motorbikes, racing cars — you're really out here being wild.
context: 丫 is northern (especially Beijing) street slang for "you/that guy", usually teasing rather than hostile. 燥 comes from rock culture, where it means a crowd going wild, and here stands in for the dialect word 作 (to make a fuss, stir things up). The phrase broke out in the first half of 2026 through short videos and comment sections, becoming an all-purpose reaction to anyone being extra; some users have criticised it as coarse.

meaning: A viral self-soothing trick: instead of sighing downward with your head bowed and shoulders slumped (which feels like giving up), lift your head, open your chest and let the sigh rise — the end of the sigh pitched upward ('唉↗'). People share it as a tiny ritual for releasing a bad mood, and half-jokingly claim it brings better luck.
meaning_zh: 网络流行的解压小技巧：不再低头弓背地往下叹气，而是抬头挺胸、尾音上扬（“唉↗”），把闷气往上吐出去。网友把它当作释放坏情绪、和自己和解的小仪式，还半开玩笑地说“叹气要往上叹，不然运气会越来越不好”。
example: 心情不好的时候别老低头叹气，试试向上叹气，据说真的有用。
example_pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou bié lǎo dītóu tànqì, shìshì xiàng shàng tànqì, jùshuō zhēn de yǒuyòng.
example_translation: When you're feeling down, don't just sigh with your head bowed — try sighing upward instead, apparently it actually works.
context: It spread on Weibo and Douyin from around May 2026, when posts under the hashtag #当我学会了向上叹气# framed the upward sigh as a gentle way for adults to soothe themselves. By June people were adding a mock-superstitious twist — sigh upward or your luck will keep getting worse — and by August it had settled into everyday self-talk for small frustrations like early classes and unfinished homework.

meaning: The hook of a deliberately absurd, catchy rap freestyle that exploded into a nationwide meme. The lyrics just repeat 'Chinese people can fly, yellow skin is right, only flies in Chinese, China is beautiful' — nonsensical on its face, but netizens read it as both tongue-in-cheek national pride (rockets, space stations, big planes — 'we can fly') and a generically hype self-affirmation chant.
meaning_zh: 一段刻意荒诞、洗脑的说唱即兴哼唱爆红成为全网热梗，歌词反复唱'中国人能飞，黄皮肤才对，讲中文才飞，中国就是美'。表面无厘头，但网友们既读出了民族自豪感（卫星、飞船、空间站、大飞机都能'飞'上天），也当作一句万能的自我打气口号来玩梗。
example: 面试通过了！中国人能飞！
example_pinyin: Miànshì tōngguò le! Zhōngguó rén néng fēi!
example_translation: Passed the interview! Chinese people can fly!
context: Huizhou rapper 揽佬 (real name 陈序垲) performed it as a freestyle on the US rap radio show *On The Radar* on 18 July 2026, singing in his Huizhou-accented Mandarin over a Memphis-style beat that samples K-391's 'Summertime'. It stayed a niche rap-circle oddity until 28 July, when 《国防时报》 used it as the soundtrack for a video of rockets and fighter jets — the moment it broke out. It hit Weibo's trending list on 5 August, and remixes setting the hook to all kinds of footage racked up millions of plays on Bilibili, making it one of the summer's biggest earworm memes.

meaning: A viral 'choice → praise' template that began with a house cat being shown a carrot and a tissue and asked to pick, then getting cooed at with '真棒!' (so good!) no matter what it chose. Netizens turned the format into a meme applied to any scenario where someone is comically unable to tell two things apart — recast with stereotypes like 'women who can't identify car logos' or 'men who can't tell skincare products apart'.
meaning_zh: 源自宠物博主给猫做'选择题'的视频——猫听不懂胡萝卜和纸巾的区别，全靠看主人表情语气选，选完不管对错都被夸'真棒！'。这套'出题→选择→夸奖'的框架被网友套用到各种'分不清'的场景里，比如'女生认不出车标''男生分不清化妆品'，迅速蔓延到职场、教育、美妆等各个领域。
example: 这波操作简直是萝卜纸巾——瞎选一个，反正都夸真棒。
example_pinyin: Zhè bō cāozuò jiǎnzhí shì luóbo zhǐjīn — xiā xuǎn yī gè, fǎnzhèng dōu kuā zhēn bàng.
example_translation: This whole thing is basically carrot-or-tissue — just pick one blindly, you'll get praised either way.
context: The format started with a cat named 大开门 in a pet-training video from late 2025, where the owner held up a carrot and a tissue and let the cat 'choose' by reading its owner's tone and face rather than actually distinguishing the objects — every choice got a '真棒!' (so good!). It became one of 2026's first big viral memes, and creators started applying the same 'impossible choice, guaranteed praise' structure to send up all kinds of situations, especially ones that stereotype people as unable to tell superficially similar things apart.

meaning: A classical fable-turned-idiom for someone who rigidly applies an old rule to a changed situation — like the man who dropped his sword overboard, carved a notch on the boat to mark the spot, and later dove in at the notch even though the boat (and the sword) had long since moved. Used online to call out anyone — a policy, a boss, a strategy — that refuses to adapt when circumstances have shifted.
meaning_zh: 出自《吕氏春秋》的寓言：楚人剑掉入江中，在船舷刻记号，船靠岸后却按刻痕处下水找剑——殊不知船已经移动，剑早不在原处了。现多用来批评那些不知变通、死守旧规矩、忽视客观情况已经改变的人或做法。
example: 都什么年代了还用老办法管新团队，这不是刻舟求剑吗？
example_pinyin: Dōu shénme niándài le hái yòng lǎo bànfǎ guǎn xīn tuánduì, zhè bù shì kè zhōu qiú jiàn ma?
example_translation: It's a different era now and you're still managing the new team with old methods — isn't that just marking the boat to find the sword?
context: One of the oldest fables in the Chinese school curriculum (from 《吕氏春秋·察今》), but it stays alive in comment sections precisely because it's such a compact put-down: people reach for it whenever someone applies an outdated rulebook — a manager's playbook, an investor's old thesis, a parent's fixed idea of 'how things are done' — to a situation that has since changed underneath them.

literal: "Ma" (surname) + holiday — a pun on a celebrity's given name
meaning: A homophone meme on idol 马嘉祺's name: his given name 嘉祺 (Jiāqí) sounds like 假期 (jiàqī, 'holiday'), and with his surname 马 ('horse') landing in the 2026 Year of the Horse, fans and workers joked that every holiday in the Horse year is a '马假期' — a Ma Jiaqi. Used as a tongue-in-cheek charm for wishing yourself more time off.
meaning_zh: 谐音梗：偶像马嘉祺的名字“嘉祺”与“假期”同音，又姓“马”，正逢2026马年，网友便调侃“马年的每个假期都是马嘉祺”，简称“马假期”。常被打工人拿来祈求多放几天假。
example: 十一马上到了，马年的每个假期都是马嘉祺，这个马假期我一定要好好过！
example_pinyin: Shíyī mǎshàng dào le, mǎ nián de měi gè jiàqī dōu shì Mǎ Jiāqí, zhège Mǎ jiàqī wǒ yídìng yào hǎohǎo guò!
example_translation: National Day is almost here — every holiday in the Year of the Horse is a Ma Jiaqi, and I'm going to make the most of this 'Ma holiday'!
context: Fans were already punning 嘉祺/假期 around TNT (时代少年团) concert promotion before the May Day holiday in 2025. With the Year of the Horse approaching, the joke became 'every holiday in the Horse year is a Ma Jiaqi', and at Weibo Night on 5 February 2026 he cheerfully said the line himself, pushing the pun from fandom into general holiday chatter.
